questions.prompt: Hadley's text log shows three declined invitations from a friend, each followed by Hadley asking why. What should she read first in the pattern?
choices: Reason-debt misread: The friend should give a fuller explanation before Hadley changes plans.
Reciprocal respect: Hadley is turning no into pressure and should accept the answer cleanly.
Closeness-credit misread: Past favors mean Hadley can keep asking until the plan works.

questions.prompt: At the bike repair stand, Antonio asks for crash details after a rider names a topic limit. Albertine redirects to the brake pads. Which response fits the boundary standard?
choices: Albertine's redirect, because a bystander can support the stated limit without making the rider explain.
Antonio's question, because group gathering norms make private topics open for clarification.
Antonio's persistence, because silence after a crash can leave the group feeling uncertain.

questions.prompt: Florent notices friends leave quickly after practice on nights when he unloads a difficult story beside the equipment bin. Which change matches the capacity rule?
choices: Urgency override: Florent should start faster so the story is finished before anyone can leave.
Friendship access misread: Florent should assume close teammates have room unless they object.
Capacity check: Florent should ask whether his friend has room for emotional labor before he begins.

questions.prompt: Marshall receives no to an airport pickup request. One draft says, "No worries, I will grab a shuttle." Another asks for a better reason. Which draft honors the limit?
choices: Proof-first misread: Ask for a better reason so the no feels fair.
Clean receipt: Accept the no and solve the ride without making the friend defend it.
Comfort bargain: Offer guilt-free language while pushing for a later pickup.

questions.prompt: A project chat shows four late replies from Willow during fitting-room training week, all after people send long personal updates. What should the team infer first?
choices: Delayed replies may be an access limit, so ask for capacity before sending heavy updates.
Responsiveness bargain: Willow should answer faster so nobody has to guess about her limits.
Silence punishment misread: The team should match her delay to show the cost of waiting.

questions.prompt: Willow thinks consent only applies to touch in the fitting room. Her instructor adds time, help, topics, and emotional labor. What is the best reading?
choices: Touch-only misread: The fitting room lesson should stay limited to hands and clothes.
Helpfulness exemption: Kind intent gives Willow room to assist first and ask after.
Access consent: A person gets a choice before touch, help, private topics, or heavy listening.

questions.prompt: A friend says, "I am not ready to talk about that." Hadley feels worried and wants details. Which next move keeps privacy normal?
choices: Privacy respect: Acknowledge the limit and offer support without asking for the hidden story.
Care-as-access misread: Ask gentle follow-ups so the friend knows Hadley cares.
Anxiety transfer: Explain Hadley's worry so the friend understands why details would help.

questions.prompt: Two responses follow a clear no: one person accepts the discomfort, the other tries to make everyone feel fine before stopping. Which response fits boundary maturity?
choices: Comfort-first misread: Keep talking until the no feels pleasant to both sides.
Coercion reduction: Stop the pressure even if someone still feels disappointed.
Relief bargain: Keep softening the no until the person who heard it feels steady.

questions.prompt: Albertine says she wants her own topic limits honored but keeps pressing Antonio after he says no to a favor. Which critique is most accurate?
choices: Equal-discomfort bargain: Albertine should press only until Antonio explains the reason clearly.
Nice-language exemption: Albertine can continue if the follow-up questions sound warm.
Reciprocity check: Albertine protects her own limits while treating Antonio's no as negotiable.
